scope: Proposition 6.5 (Groups and numerical bounds) of the manuscript “Elliptic squares and Zilber–Pink for curves in A2” (preprints/Elliptic-Squares-and-Zilber-Pink-for-Curves-in-A2-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 016 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 d3ecf115570d0b89), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 39. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There are fixed constants C such that either h ≤ CdC, or there is one system of type (1), (2) or (3), with (6.9), having the following properties. Its target is an algebraic point z = (a, U) in an affine space of fixed dimension, and it holds at all embeddings in a weighted subcollection V ⊂ V0. Writing each scalar expression as E(a, U) = ∑ j≥0 aj ej(U), the numerical and function hypotheses of Theorem 2.1 hold: haff(z) ≤ CdC h, ∑ v∈V wv log 1 |a|v ≥ h CdC , (6.10) ∑ v∈V wv log+ ∥U∥v ≤ CdC (1 + log h)C , deg ej ≤ C(1 + j), (6.11) haff(ej) ≤ C(1 + j + d)C (1 + log h)C , (6.12) ⏐ ⏐ ⏐ ⏐ ⏐ ⏐ ∑ j≥l aj ej(U) ⏐ ⏐ ⏐ ⏐ ⏐ ⏐ v ≤ |a|l v exp ( (1 + l)bv ) , ∑ v∈V wvbv ≤ CdC (1 + log h)C . (6.13) Here l ≥ 0, bv ≥ 0, and one common choice of bv works for the bounded number of expressions. Each expression is a polynomial combination of fixed bounded degree of the coordinates, fixed regular algebraic germs and fixed ordinary horizontal matrix germs, evaluated at a and, in type (2), at aR. Only a fixed finite list of such germs is used. Constants in the expressions may depend on the target, with the bounds displayed above. There are at most CdC groups in the construction. This bound counts ordered conjugate tuples, not elements of the Galois group of a normal closure. The proposition asserts no nonidentity condition on an algebraic subvariety through z.
